capabilities.text: Authenticate ward nurses via Azure AD single sign-on (SSO) to access the app.
Display a real-time, mobile-responsive patient roster for the nurse's current shift, loading within 3 seconds and caching data locally for 5 minutes.
Allow ward nurses to select a patient from their roster and enter free-text clinical notes with auto-save every 30 seconds.
Provide a predefined dropdown for nurses to select note types (e.g., Vital Signs, Medication Change, Behavioral Concern) when entering notes.
Submit clinical notes to the Epic EMR system via FHIR STU3 API with OAuth 2.0 client credentials through Azure API Management.
Automatically queue and retry note submissions if Epic is unreachable, retrying every 30 seconds with exponential backoff for up to 15 minutes.
Notify nurses in-app and via push notification if note sync to Epic fails after retry period, allowing manual retry.
Allow nurses to save notes locally for patients marked as transferred or discharged, tagging notes as local-only and purging them after 7 days unless reviewed.
Enable charge nurses to view a real-time dashboard of all ward notes with color-coded sync status and alert-flagged notes, auto-refreshing every 2 minutes.
Allow charge nurses to export the dashboard overview to PDF, sending it securely via encrypted email with audit logging of exports.
Provide a secure admin portal for clinical informatics leads to audit note distribution, duplication rates, and review local-only notes.
Support full offline note creation and editing on the nurse's device using IndexedDB and service workers, with conflict resolution based on timestamps.
Restrict access to alert-flagged notes to only pharmacy liaisons and charge nurses, requiring audit-logged reasons for each access.
Provide a curated alert dashboard view for pharmacy liaisons showing only notes flagged with alerts, with automated escalation via Microsoft Teams and ServiceNow.
Allow charge nurses and clinical informatics leads to review local-only notes and either release them to Epic or mark them as reviewed to prevent purging.
Enforce role-based access control using Azure AD app roles mapped to user roles, with multi-factor authentication required for all users.
Store patient notes, local-only note queue, and audit events securely in Azure SQL Database with encryption at rest and row-level security.
Retain patient notes and audit logs for 7 years in Azure SQL, then archive notes to immutable Azure Blob Storage for an additional 10 years.
Ensure the React frontend communicates only with the .NET backend API, which handles all calls to Epic and ward shift systems, preventing exposure of FHIR credentials in the browser.
Display shift summary to ward nurses at shift end showing all submitted notes with sync status, allowing manual retry of failed notes and export to PDF.
